· Passive voice: "Admittance was refused to him by Mr. Amar."

· Past tense of 'refused' remains in the past form in passive construction.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. The summer was ______ hot this year.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.

The summer was ______ hot this year.
questions.solution:
· Correct sentence: "The summer was too hot this year."

· Too: Means "excessively" or "more than needed."

· Tow: Means pulling something.

· Two: The number 2.

· To: Preposition, incorrect in this context.

O. want

S. the
questions.solution:

o Q: "Do you"

o O: "want"

S) bold
questions.solution: (R) should start with "Fortune" because it is the subject. (P) always favours - This follows logically, as "Fortune always favours" is a common phrase. (Q) modifies the object of the sentence. (S) is the final phrase that completes the sentence meaningfully.

questions.question: In the question, four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word. It was as if the newer hybrids had an insatiable appetite for chemicals.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question, four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word.

It was as if the newer hybrids had an insatiable appetite for chemicals.
questions.solution:
· Insatiable means impossible to satisfy or fulfill.

· Satisfiable (Correct Answer): Opposite of "insatiable," meaning "capable of being satisfied."

· Urgent: Incorrect, means "requiring immediate attention."

· Curbed: Means "restricted" but does not convey the exact opposite of "insatiable."

· Pressing: Means "demanding quick attention," which is unrelated to the context.

questions.question: Select the correctly spelled word to fill in the blank. My grandmother ________________ the preparation of every festival celebration in my house.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correctly spelled word to fill in the blank.

My grandmother ________________ the preparation of every festival celebration in my house.
questions.solution:
· Correct spelling: "initiates" → Means "begins or starts something."

· All other options are misspellings.

questions.question: Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence in the correct order. P. and has also created a wide gap between them Q. laid too much stress on R. teachers and students S. online mode of education has
questions.questionHtml:
Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence in the correct order.

P. and has also created a wide gap between them

Q. laid too much stress on

R. teachers and students

S. online mode of education has
questions.solution:
· SQRP forms the meaningful sentence:

"The online mode of education has laid too much stress on teachers and students and has also created a wide gap between them."

· SRPQ: Incorrect, as "teachers and students" should come after mentioning stress in education.

· RQPS: Incorrect, as it starts with "teachers and students" without context.

· PSQR: Incorrect, as "and has also created" should not begin the sentence.

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. He always wants to be in the company of those who are intellectually superior than him.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.

He always wants to be in the company of those who are intellectually superior than him.
questions.solution:
· Error: "superior than him" → The word "superior" is a comparative adjective that does not require "than."

· Correction: "superior to him."

· Other options are grammatically correct.

questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error. I have sing 'Let It Go' before a crowd of thousands of people.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.

I have sing 'Let It Go' before a crowd of thousands of people.
questions.solution:
· Error: "I have sing" → Incorrect verb form.

· Correction: "I have sung 'Let It Go' before a crowd of thousands of people."

· "Have" requires past participle (sung), not base form (sing).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Aesthetic value is specifically a way in which we can get positive conclude value from the world at large.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Aesthetic value is specifically a way in which we can get positive conclude value from the world at large.
questions.solution:
· Error: "conclude value" → Incorrect usage.

· Correction: "conclusive value" → Correct, meaning "definitive or meaningful value."

· Other options (convalescent, convulsive, contrastive) do not fit the context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Purify
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Purify
questions.solution:
· Purify means "to make clean or remove impurities."

· Pollute (Correct Answer): Means "to make dirty or contaminate," which is the opposite of purify.

· Chant: Unrelated, means "to recite or sing rhythmically."

· Invite: Means "to request someone's presence," unrelated to purification.

· Wash: Similar to "purify," not an antonym.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Left out in the cold
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Left out in the cold
questions.solution:
· Left out in the cold means to be excluded or ignored from a group, decision, or event.

· To go underground: Means to hide secretly, often for safety.

· To be in hiding: Similar to option 1, but does not relate to the meaning of the idiom.

· To be extremely negative: Incorrect, as this does not relate to the idiom's meaning.

questions.question: Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Lady Stranleigh continued to smile at him brilliantly .
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Lady Stranleigh continued to smile at him brilliantly.
questions.solution:
· Brilliantly means shining brightly or done in an impressive way.

· Dimly (Correct Answer): Opposite of "brilliantly," meaning "not bright, dull."

· Brightly: Synonym, not an antonym.

· Cunningly: Incorrect, means "in a clever or deceitful way."

· Strangely: Unrelated to brightness or brilliance.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The mothers, who suffer from postpartum depression, feel ______ by their children. (vexed)
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

The mothers, who suffer from postpartum depression, feel ______ by their children. (vexed)
questions.solution:
· Vexed means annoyed, irritated, or distressed.

· Annoyed (Correct Answer): Matches the meaning of "vexed."

· Delighted: Opposite meaning.

· Recovered: Unrelated to the meaning of "vexed."

· Pacific: Means peaceful, which is incorrect.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Trigonometry has been taught by him for donkey's years.
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
· Active voice transformation:

o Passive: "Trigonometry has been taught by him for donkey's years."

o Active: "He has been teaching trigonometry for donkey's years."

· Option 1 (He had been teaching...): Changes the tense to past perfect, incorrect.

· Option 2 (He has been trigonometry teaching...): Incorrect word order.

· Option 3 (He is teaching...): Incorrect as it changes the present perfect continuous to present continuous.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1 in the given passage.
questions.questionHtml: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1 in the given passage.
questions.solution:
· The correct word should describe music as a category or type of fine arts.

· Form (Correct Answer): Refers to a particular type or structure of art, which fits the context.

· Format: Relates to structure or arrangement, but is more relevant to documents or digital media.

· Substance: Refers to material or essence, not suitable for describing a category of art.

· Design: Related to visual structure, inappropriate for describing music.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2 in the given passage.
questions.questionHtml: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2 in the given passage.
questions.solution:
· The sentence suggests that mastering fine art is challenging.

· Difficult (Correct Answer): Fits the meaning of being hard to master.

· Irksome: Means annoying or irritating, which does not fit.

· Serious: Does not convey the difficulty of learning an art.

· Easy: Opposite of the required meaning.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3 in the given passage.
questions.questionHtml: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3 in the given passage.
questions.solution:
· The correct word should indicate revealing or expressing emotions.

· Bring (Correct Answer): "Bring out" means to reveal or make apparent.

· Catalyse: Means to speed up a reaction, which is not relevant to emotions.

· Yield: Means to produce something but does not fit well in the context.

· Effect: Means to cause a change but does not work grammatically in this sentence.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4 in the given passage.
questions.questionHtml: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4 in the given passage.
questions.solution:
· The sentence suggests that listening to music leads to humming or singing.

· Or (Correct Answer): Used for alternatives or choices, making it the right fit.

· Neither/Nor: Used for negative statements, which does not apply here.

· Either: Used when referring to two options, but it would require "either... or" structure, which is absent.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5 in the given passage.
questions.questionHtml: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5 in the given passage.
questions.solution:
· The sentence implies that singing is highly refined and requires training, meaning it is complex.

· Intricate (Correct Answer): Means "highly detailed, complex, and requiring skill."

· Uncomplicated: Opposite of the intended meaning.

· Uniform: Means consistent, which does not fit the context.

· Mixed: Refers to a combination of things, irrelevant here.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A thing that can be easily carried by hands
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A thing that can be easily carried by hands
questions.solution:
· Portable (Correct Answer): Means easily carried or moved, especially by hand.

· Export: Means sending goods to another country.

· Import: Means bringing goods into a country.

· Potable: Means safe to drink (often confused with portable).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Break the ice
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Break the ice

options.text: Ill-feeling carried by a person over a period of time
options.html: Ill-feeling carried by a person over a period of time

options.text: To say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed, especially at the beginning of a meeting or party
options.html: To say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed, especially at the beginning of a meeting or party

questions.solution:
· Break the ice means to initiate conversation or ease tension in a social situation.

· Option 1 (Nervousness) → Incorrect, refers to "stage fright."

· Option 2 (Ill-feeling over time) → Incorrect, means "grudge" instead.

· Option 3 (Respect for achievements) → Incorrect, refers to admiration.
